Consequences for a third party: the `--run` stage of six studies is unreproducible without repeating ~5 hours of MPS compute plus live ColabFold MSA-server calls, and — more seriously — none of the derived per-fold numbers in data/study_*.json can be independently re-derived from committed structures, so the analysis layer must be trusted rather than checked. The rescue_runs.py mechanism that solved exactly this problem for the first 24 runs was never applied to the studies.
findings.fix: Run platform/rescue_runs.py (extended with the six study work directories) to content-address the study artefacts into runs/ with sha256 entries in runs/manifest.json. Full mmCIF sets are too large for git, so commit the confidence JSON, the per-fold ipTM/pLDDT/PAE summaries and the sha256 of every structure file, and deposit the structures themselves in Zenodo with the DOI recorded in runs/manifest.json — that keeps the repo small while making every published number checkable against a fixed artefact.

findings.title: verify_all.py mutates a tracked file, and the committed data/dataset.json is stale relative to HEAD
findings.location: platform/build_dataset.py (writes data/dataset.json with a git_sha field); verify_all.py:36; data/dataset.json
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/scratch/clean && git status --short && python3 verify_all.py >/dev/null 2>&1 && git status --short && git diff data/dataset.json | head -20 && cd /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio && git rev-parse --short HEAD && git status --short
findings.observed: Clean clone before: no output. After `python3 verify_all.py`: ` M data/dataset.json`, with diff `- "git_sha": "a514a1a"` / `+ "git_sha": "c28b768"`. HEAD is `c28b768`, so the committed dataset records the *previous* commit. The author's own working tree shows the same ` M data/dataset.json`.
findings.why_wrong: Running the repository's own verification dirties the working tree, so "clone, verify, confirm git is clean" — the standard reviewer check — fails. The committed build artefact also carries a git_sha that is structurally guaranteed to be one commit behind, since the sha is only knowable after the commit that contains the file. Any reader who uses data/dataset.json's git_sha to identify the code that produced it will land on the wrong commit.
findings.fix: Either drop data/dataset.json from version control (add it to .gitignore, generate it at setup) or make build_dataset.py write the sha of HEAD~0 at build time into an untracked sidecar (data/dataset.build.json) while keeping the tracked dataset byte-stable. Add a CI step asserting `git diff --quiet` after verify_all.py so the invariant is enforced rather than assumed.

unverified_concerns: Whether the .agents/skills/ tree is byte-identical to upstream google-deepmind/science-skills. I verified the declared source (skills-lock.json), the retained per-file Apache headers (64 files match 'Copyright 2026 Google LLC'), and that upstream's LICENSE is Apache-2.0, but I did not diff the vendored files against upstream, so I cannot say whether they are modified (Apache-2.0 §4(b) would then additionally require change notices).

Whether the GitHub copy at hopejsh/CognitionBioChem has a LICENSE added out-of-band through the GitHub UI. My checks were against the local clone and its git history only; `git ls-files` at HEAD shows none, but I did not fetch the public repo.

Whether the ADMET, PRODIGY and PoseBusters code paths run correctly from a clean install. verify_all.py does not exercise them, and I deliberately did not install admet-ai/torch (multi-GB) into the clean checkout, so their dependency surface is inferred from imports rather than executed.

Whether the published site (GitHub Pages or equivalent) actually serves index.html with the contradictory disclosure. I confirmed the string in the committed HTML, the committed dataset and the renderer in app.js, but inspected no deployment.

Reproducibility of the `--run` stage for studies #9 and #10. I honoured the instruction not to re-run Boltz, so my clean-checkout evidence covers `--register` and `--analyse` only; #10 additionally needs live ColabFold MSA-server calls, which introduces a network dependency whose stability over time I did not assess.

Whether data/study_*.json can be re-derived from the /tmp working directories that still exist on this machine. I did not attempt it, so I cannot say whether the analysis code would reproduce the committed result files byte-for-byte from raw folds.
what_is_sound: All 8 pre-registration hashes verify independently from a clean checkout. I reimplemented the hash from scratch (sha256 over `json.dumps(content, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'))`) rather than calling the project's own method, and got `verified 8 mismatched 0` — every filename short hash and every stored full hash matches its content. The hash-locking is real, not decorative.

Every one of the 8 studies' `--analyse` stage runs from a pristine clone with only the four README-declared packages, and reproduces the README's numbers exactly. Slate #10 as printed by the clean checkout: `mean paired (native - own decoy mean) = 0.0186   paired t p = 0.76814   Cohen's dz = 0.1271`, `mean native ipTM 0.6244 vs mean decoy 0.6058`, `mean rise over study #9's single-sequence run: 0.2194`, decoy maxima 0.9345 / 0.8561 / 0.8261 / 0.7784 — matching README's 0.019, 0.77, 0.13, 0.624, 0.606, +0.219, 0.934, 0.856, 0.826, 0.778. The analysis layer is genuinely reproducible and the README numbers are not rounded in a flattering direction.

The pre-registration audit fires correctly on a clean checkout and reports deviations against the reader rather than hiding them: `n_observed=65 differs from n_planned=66` (#10), `n_observed=12 differs from n_planned=16` (#6), `n_observed=15 differs from n_planned=17` (#1), `n_observed=14 differs from n_planned=15` (#8), plus #7's declared DockQ chain-mapping deviation with its measured justification. Three studies return CONFIRMATORY with no deviation.

Once the single missing package is added, verify_all.py exits 0 with `113 passed, 0 failed` from a clone that has never run anything before. There is no hidden state, no ordering dependency, and no artefact from an earlier step required — the suites do not depend on outputs the repo fails to commit.

The deliberate inversion is encoded honestly in code, not just in prose: verify_all.py:32-35 declares the data gate's expected exit as 1, and the gate behaves identically from a clean checkout (`exit 1 (expected 1)`, 124 violations). A reviewer can see that the failing gate is designed rather than broken without taking anyone's word for it.

.gitignore is correct and effective: `git ls-files | grep -cE '^\.venv|^memory/index/'` returns 0. The three venvs, the derived memory index, sqlite/npz artefacts and the large raw review transcripts are all excluded, while the authoritative append-only ledger under memory/ledger/ is tracked — which is the right side of that line.

No secrets are committed. A scan for api_key/secret/token/password/Bearer/sk-/ghp_/AKIA patterns across all tracked non-vendored files returned only false positives (chemistry prose about SMILES tokens, FTS5 tokenizers, and 'acetylcholine secretion'). The only email addresses in the whole tree are two public EBI curator addresses (goa@ebi.ac.uk, dbinns@ebi.ac.uk) inside vendored reference material.

The git history is honest across all 14 commits. I diffed the file lists of 13 of them against their messages and found no mismatch: each Slate commit contains exactly its study module, its prespec file, its data/study_*.json, its ledger entries and its README section. The fabrication history is preserved rather than rewritten — the initial commit still reads 'NeuroCognition BioChem AlphaFold3 Platform' and 6d67e1e still reads 'Replace fabricated data with real computation', so a reader can reconstruct what was retracted and when.

platform/studies/peptide_interface.py is the model the other studies should copy: it has a `--curate` step (line 83, `SET.write_text(...)`) that writes its benchmark set to the tracked `data/peptide_benchmark_set.json`, so study #7's input set — unlike #1, #2, #6 and #11's — is fully in version control.
The repository is small enough to clone comfortably (14 MB .git, largest tracked file 1.2 MB), so the reproducibility problems are all fixable by addition rather than by restructuring.
audits.verdict:
NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM A CLEAN PUBLIC CHECKOUT AS IT STANDS, AND NOT LEGALLY REDISTRIBUTABLE — but the distance to fixing both is short, and the scientific core is in better shape than the packaging.

What I actually got from a fresh clone: following the README's own quick start verbatim, `verify_all.py` exits 1 with 5/6 suites (one undeclared package, biopython). Adding that one package gives 113/113 and exit 0 with no other hidden state. All eight studies' `--analyse` stages then reproduce the README's published numbers exactly, and all eight pre-registration hashes recompute from scratch. So the analysis layer and the pre-registration machinery are sound; what fails is packaging, licensing, and custody of inputs.

Ordered list of what must be added, most urgent first.

1. LICENSE + NOTICE (legal blocker, blocks everything else). The repo is public with no licence file, so the author's own 12,077 lines are all-rights-reserved and nobody may legally run them — while 229 vendored files (22,469 lines, 65% of the repo's Python) are Apache-2.0 and copyrighted Google LLC, redistributed under a blanket "Private research. © 2026 Seung H. Jung". Add a root LICENSE, a NOTICE crediting google-deepmind/science-skills, and either remove `.agents/` from version control (preferred — nothing in verify_all.py touches it) or ship the Apache-2.0 copy its own file headers point at.

2. Fix the contradictory public disclosure. data/dataset.json and index.html:28 both tell every visitor "No structure prediction has been run in this repository" while README.md:18 says Boltz-2 "produced every structure in runs/". Rewrite build_dataset.py:206-215 and the index.html fallback, and add a verify_frontend.py assertion tying the two together so they cannot drift again.

3. requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / lock files — three of them, one per environment (main numpy>=2, boltz numpy 1.26.4, dockq numpy<2), pinned to the versions the published numbers were produced with, plus `requires-python`. Right now the only record of the environment is conflicting prose inside research JSON (biopython 1.84 vs 1.88).

4. Add `biopython` to the documented install list. One line; it is the entire difference between a red and a green clean-checkout run.

5. Commit the study input sets. Four studies read inputs that exist only in /tmp and that no code path can regenerate: `/tmp/posebench_set.json` (#6 — this file *is* the benchmark and its stratification), `/tmp/ache_bench.json` and `/tmp/ache_mature.txt` (#1, #2, #8), `/tmp/cbc_variance` (#11's input structures). Move them to `data/` and add `--curate` steps, following the pattern peptide_interface.py already gets right.

6. Take custody of the study artefacts. runs/ holds 24 pre-slate runs (4.1 MB); the ~1.65 GB behind Slates #2, #6, #7, #9, #10 and #11 sits in /tmp, which the project's own rescue_runs.py:5 notes macOS may delete on reboot. Extend rescue_runs.py to those six work directories, commit confidence JSON + per-fold summaries + sha256 of every structure, and deposit the structures in Zenodo with the DOI in runs/manifest.json.

7. Document the third environment (.venvdockq / DockQ 2.1.3) that study #7 hard-requires and the README never mentions, and de-hardcode `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12/...`.

8. Make verification tree-clean. `verify_all.py` rewrites tracked data/dataset.json (its git_sha is structurally always one commit stale — a514a1a at HEAD c28b768). Untrack it or write the sha to a sidecar, then assert `git diff --quiet` in CI.

9. Scrub the 179 `/Users/seunghojung` occurrences and 8 dead scratchpad references from 14 tracked files, and add a grep guard.

10. Add CI that clones fresh, installs from requirements.txt and runs verify_all.py, so the "6 suites passing" badge is produced by the clean-checkout path it advertises. Then a CITATION.cff, since seven hash-locked pre-registered studies deserve to be citable.

Items 1, 3, 4 and 5 are what a JOSS review would hold the submission on. Items 2 and 6 are what an adversarial reader would hold it on. Nothing here impugns the science: the numbers I could check reproduced exactly, the deviations are self-reported, and the git history is honest about the fabrication it was built to correct.

The disclaimer at README.md:571 cannot cure either, because it lives inside a file the description does not travel with. A careful 500-line disclosure document is fully undercut by a 96-character subtitle.

README.md:12 badge: license-private_research
findings.why_wrong: Two distinct problems. First, with no licence, default copyright applies: every visitor gets exclusive-rights-reserved code. They may view and fork within GitHub under the GitHub ToS, but they may not copy, run, modify, or redistribute it. For a project whose entire value proposition is reproducibility — 8 hash-locked pre-registrations, 145 content-addressed artefacts, six verification suites — this makes lawful reproduction impossible for everyone. "Private research" is not an OSI licence, has no defined terms, and grants nothing. Second, and more seriously, the repository is 43% third-party content (LIC-02) plus ChEMBL and UniProt data carrying inbound copyleft and attribution conditions. Asserting blanket private ownership over that composite misstates the rights position: those inbound licences require permissions to be passed through, not withdrawn.
findings.fix: Decide and publish an outbound licence. Recommended split, which is compatible with every inbound obligation found here: (a) /LICENSE = Apache-2.0 covering platform/, verify_all.py, app.js, index.html — Apache-2.0 is required in any case by LIC-02 and is compatible with the MIT, BSD and MPL dependencies; (b) /LICENSE-DATA = CC BY-SA 4.0 covering data/ — CC BY-SA 4.0 is the one-way-compatible upgrade path from ChEMBL's CC BY-SA 3.0 and satisfies UniProt's CC BY 4.0; (c) state the split in README.md and replace the badge. Remove the phrase "Private research" — it is inaccurate on a public repository and inconsistent with the inbound terms.

CC BY-SA 3.0 s4(a): "You must include a copy of, or the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) for, this License with every copy of the Work You Distribute". s4(c) requires keeping intact all copyright notices and providing the name of the Original Author, the title of the Work, and the URI.
findings.why_wrong: Distribution has already occurred — the files are committed and the repository is public — so ss4(a) and 4(c) are live and breached. Both are unconditional: they apply whether the committed file is treated as a Collection or an Adaptation, so the classification question does not need to be settled for the breach to exist. On share-alike (s4(b)), my assessment is that data/corpus_ACHE.json is more likely an Adaptation than a Collection, because it recasts ChEMBL records into a new schema and interleaves them with locally computed descriptors rather than including them "in its entirety in unmodified form"; if so it must itself be distributed under CC BY-SA 3.0 or a compatible later version. I flag that this specific point is genuinely contestable and a rights-holder could see it either way. What is not contestable: share-alike, if it attaches, attaches to the data files, NOT to the repository as a whole — it does not make platform/*.py copyleft, and any advice that says otherwise is overreach. Note also that the underlying measured values are facts, not copyrightable in the US; the EU sui generis database right is unlikely to bite at 18 compounds out of ChEMBL's millions. The realistic exposure is a licence-condition breach and the reputational cost of an unattributed EMBL-EBI extract, not litigation.

unverified_concerns: Whether data/corpus_ACHE.json legally constitutes an "Adaptation" (triggering CC BY-SA 3.0 s4(b) share-alike) or a "Collection" (attribution only) is a question of copyright law I cannot settle by running a command. My assessment is that it leans Adaptation, because the file recasts ChEMBL records into a bespoke schema interleaved with locally computed descriptors rather than including them unmodified. LIC-05 is therefore written so the required remedy rests on ss4(a) and 4(c), which are breached either way. A qualified IP lawyer should confirm the share-alike scope before the data licence is finalised.

Whether EMBL-EBI would treat an 18-compound / 27-activity extract as engaging the EU sui generis database right (Directive 96/9/EC Art. 7) — either as a "substantial part" or as repeated systematic extraction of insubstantial parts under Art. 7(5)). I judge this unlikely at this scale against a multi-million-record database, but I did not verify EBI's own position and did not contact them.

Whether ChEMBL's own upstream contributors impose terms beyond CC BY-SA 3.0 on the specific assay records committed (the 14 assay and 12 document accessions in data/corpus_ACHE.json trace to primary literature under publisher copyright). I retrieved ChEMBL's blanket licence but did not check any individual source publication's terms.

Whether the 145 artefacts in runs/ contain any Boltz-2 training-data residue that could carry third-party terms. I verified the committed .cif files are Boltz outputs declaring `_struct.pdbx_structure_determination_methodology computational` and referencing the PDB Chemical Component Dictionary (CC0), but I did not audit the Boltz-2 weights' training corpus, and I did not re-run any prediction.

Whether the GitHub repository has a social-preview image, wiki, Discussions, or Releases carrying further claims or third-party content. I audited the API description, topics, homepage and has_pages fields only; has_pages was false and homepage null.

Whether git history contains third-party data in commits now removed from HEAD. I audited the working tree and the tracked file set at HEAD; a public repository exposes full history, so a `git log -p` review for previously committed data would be prudent before any licence is applied retroactively.

The task brief states "113 platform checks"; verify_all.py reports 109 for the platform regression suite. I did not investigate the discrepancy because the README itself makes no such claim, so there is nothing in the repository to correct.
what_is_sound: PDB redistribution hygiene is genuinely exemplary, and it is the single best-handled source here. `find . -name '*.cif' -o -name '*.pdb' | grep -v boltz_results` returns nothing outside the venvs — not one experimental coordinate file is committed, tracked or untracked. All 24 tracked .cif files are Boltz-2 outputs. What is committed from the PDB is metadata: 16 IDs, deposition dates, resolutions, sequences and struct.title strings. RCSB releases the core archive under CC0 1.0, so there is no legal obligation at all here; the missing PDB citation is a courtesy, not a breach.

The 16 benchmark PDB IDs are real and the metadata is accurate. I spot-checked five against the live RCSB API (10LG, 21EE, 31GN, 4S15, and 23SI from the pose-accuracy discussion): all returned HTTP 200 and titles matching the committed JSON character-for-character. The unusual-looking post-cutoff IDs (10LG, 12ZJ, 21EE, 23AG, 29TJ, 31EE, 31GN, 10TC) are legitimate recent depositions, not fabrications.

The README's Boltz licensing claim is exactly right, and I checked both halves independently. README.md:109-110 asserts "MIT licence on both code and weights"; the upstream LICENSE reads "MIT License, Copyright (c) 2024 Jeremy Wohlwend, Gabriele Corso, Saro Passaro" and the upstream README states "Our model and code are released under MIT License, and can be freely used for both academic and commercial purposes." The 145 derived artefacts in runs/ are therefore freely redistributable, and the framing at README.md:110 — "This is a licensing substitution, not a claim of scientific equivalence" — is precisely the right distinction to draw.

The AlphaFold 3 licensing analysis at README.md:104-107 checks out against the upstream repository: Apache-2.0 source, weights obtainable only directly from Google, request-restricted and non-commercial, governed by separate WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md and WEIGHTS_PROHIBITED_USE_POLICY.md documents. Choosing Boltz-2 on licensing grounds and saying so plainly is the correct call, correctly explained.

The trademark disclaimer is present and properly worded in both README.md:571-572 and index.html:250-251, using the right formula — non-affiliation, non-endorsement, and express acknowledgement that AlphaFold is a trademark of Google DeepMind. index.html:73-79 goes further and enumerates what the tool does not do, including "Claim any affiliation with Google DeepMind or the AlphaFold team." The wording itself needs no change; LIC-01 is about the surfaces it fails to reach, not its content.

platform/cbc/compute/structure.py carries machine-readable licence and citation metadata per backend — MIT plus a Wohlwend/Passaro citation for Boltz-2 at line 90, CC-BY-4.0 plus a Varadi citation for AlphaFold DB at lines 95-100, and an explicit "weights: request-only, non-commercial, non-redistributable" for AlphaFold 3. Every retrieval result is stamped with licence and citation at lines 310-311. This is better than most research code manages, and it means the fix for LIC-07 is to surface data the project already holds rather than to go and find it.

All three virtual environments are correctly excluded from version control, with .gitignore carrying an explanatory comment about the 1.6 GB of Boltz weights. `git ls-files | grep -cE '^\.venv'` returns 0, so no dependency source or model weight is redistributed by this repository, and the copyleft packages found in .venv312 create no present exposure.

All six verification suites pass as the README claims, including the data gate correctly failing by design: "[PASS] Data-integrity gate (expected to FAIL on legacy data) — exit 1 (expected 1) — 124 violations across 13 categories". The inverted-expectation gate is a genuinely good piece of design and the badge at README.md:10 describes it honestly.

The README's scientific self-disclosure is unusually candid and I found no overclaim within it — the status disclosure at lines 16-26, the retraction narrative at 30-35, the falsified hypotheses reported as falsified across slates 6 through 10, "Not one candidate beat its own null", "the model is the larger error term", and "No wet-lab validation of anything." Findings LIC-01 and LIC-11 are the only overclaims I could reproduce, and LIC-01 lives in GitHub metadata rather than in the README, which is exactly why it needs fixing: the document is honest and the subtitle is not.
audits.verdict:
Three BLOCKERs, all fixable in an afternoon, none of them scientific. The research content of this repository is honest — I went looking for residual overclaim in the README and found essentially none. The exposure is entirely in the packaging.

The most urgent item is not a licence at all. The public GitHub description reads "State-of-the-art AlphaFold3 Structural Pharmacology & De Novo Cognition-Enhancing Drug Discovery Platform" and the topics include `alphafold3` and `deepmind`. That text re-asserts, to every visitor and every search result, the two claims this project's own rebuild demolished: that it is AlphaFold3 (README.md:32 — "no AlphaFold3 existed anywhere in the codebase") and that the peptides are de novo designs (README.md:23 — "not de novo designs: no generative model produced them"). It also puts the AlphaFold mark and a DeepMind affiliation signal on the one surface the footer disclaimer cannot reach. A 500-line honest disclosure loses to a 96-character subtitle, because most people only read the subtitle.

The second is the cleanest legal breach and the one I would fix first if I could only fix one thing quietly: 229 tracked files copied from google-deepmind/science-skills — 43% of the repository — redistributed publicly with no copy of the Apache-2.0 licence and no CC BY notice on the non-code materials, against a named corporate copyright holder. Unlike the ChEMBL question, nothing about this is contestable.

The third is structural: no LICENSE file, so visitors receive all-rights-reserved code, which makes lawful reproduction impossible for a project whose entire value proposition is reproducibility — while the README simultaneously asserts "Private research" over material carrying inbound copyleft and attribution conditions.

On the specific question asked about ChEMBL share-alike: attribution under CC BY-SA 3.0 ss4(a) and 4(c) is unconditionally required and unconditionally absent, so the breach exists regardless of classification. Whether s4(b) share-alike also attaches turns on Adaptation-versus-Collection, which I judge leans Adaptation but flag as genuinely contestable. What I want to be emphatic about, because it is the most common place this analysis goes wrong: share-alike attaches to the data files, not to the repository. It does not make platform/*.py copyleft. Recommending CC BY-SA 4.0 for data/ and Apache-2.0 for code satisfies every inbound obligation found here without over-restricting the codebase.

One finding deserves separate mention because of what it reveals about how the gap opened. platform/cbc/corpus.py:12-14 states "nothing is redistributed... this module stores only identifiers plus locally computed values." That is false against the committed file — 18 ChEMBL SMILES, 18 preferred names, 26 measured standard_values — and the module's own provenance layer contradicts it three hundred lines later by tagging those fields pv.database() and pv.literature(). Meanwhile the redistributed ChEMBL skill carried a licence-notification gate that was never fired, because corpus.py calls the API directly instead of through the wrapper that would have fired it. A control existed; it was bypassed silently; a false premise then justified the omission. The durable fix is not the NOTICE file — it is adding a licence check to platform/validate.py so attribution becomes an executable gate, like the data-integrity gate and the free-energy naming guard this project already runs. This codebase is unusually good at converting standards into tests. Licensing is the one standard it left as prose.

What is genuinely sound is worth stating plainly, because it is not accidental. Not one experimental PDB coordinate file is committed — only Boltz outputs. The Boltz MIT-on-weights claim is correct, and I verified it upstream rather than taking it on trust. The AlphaFold 3 licensing analysis is accurate. The trademark disclaimer is correctly worded in both public-facing files; it simply does not reach GitHub metadata. structure.py already carries per-backend licence and citation metadata, which is better hygiene than most research code achieves and means several fixes are plumbing rather than research. Someone thought carefully about redistribution here. They then wrote that thinking into a docstring instead of a NOTICE file and a test.

findings.why_wrong: The loop iterates over every target whose alias appears anywhere in the string and then applies that target's numbering to every Xaa### token in the whole string. A binding-site string that names three proteins gets all its residues checked against each of them. Two consequences: (a) correct residues of protein X are reported as fabricated because they were resolved against protein Y — Keap1 Tyr334 and Arg415 are the canonical Kelch-domain arginine/tyrosine pair, both present in Q14145, yet the gate calls them wrong; (b) the alias 'M1' is a two-character substring that matches inside 'TM1'/'TM2'/'TM5', so any GPCR transmembrane annotation silently pulls in CHRM1. At least 12 of the 45 calls (4 Ginkgolide/CHRM1, 2 B5/CHRM1, 4 Curcumin/KEAP1, 2 Asiatic/NTRK2) are artefacts of the checker, i.e. >=27% of the largest failure category. The number 45 is published verbatim in verify_all.py:34 and README.md:254 as a scientific result about the legacy data.
findings.fix: Parse the binding-site string into target-scoped segments before resolving: split on ';' and on target-name boundaries, and check each Xaa### token only against the target named in its own segment. Anchor aliases with word boundaries (re.search(r'\bM1\b', ...)) so 'TM1' cannot match CHRM1, or drop the bare 'M1' alias in favour of 'M1 mAChR'/'CHRM1'/'muscarinic'. Re-derive and republish the 45 figure after the fix.

findings.observed: 17 candidates satisfy the stated rule, including four that are neither in CANDIDATE_TARGETS nor covered by any stated exclusion: PfcGluN2A-LTP-P3 (GRIN2A), PfcDual-nACh-GluN2A-P5 (CHRNA7, GRIN2A), BasalM1-PAM-B2 (CHRM1), AstroEaat2-Up-A2 (SLC1A2). The prespec 'exclusions' field reads verbatim: "Only the 6 candidates whose declared receptor is in the target registry AND is extracellular are screened. Candidates naming an intracellular target (Keap1, GSK-3, Nrf2, AMPK) are excluded ... Sequences containing non-standard residues are excluded." data/study_candidate_screen.json screened exactly 6.
findings.why_wrong: The stated inclusion rule is not the implemented one. The implemented rule is: (1) a hand-written 10-entry dict CANDIDATE_TARGETS, whose membership criterion is nowhere stated; then (2) sort by receptor length and take the 6 cheapest (candidate_screen.py:98-99, 'cheapest first'). Neither step appears in the hash-locked plan, and the length cut is an efficiency criterion, not a scientific one. Four qualifying candidates (P3, P5, B2, A2) and two more mapped ones (MicroTlr4-Antagonist-M3, PfcTrk-ErkEnhancer-P2, plus HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 and BasalNgf-TrkA-B3) were dropped without any registered reason. The prespec audit still prints 'confirmatory' because it does not check the exclusion text against the code.
findings.fix: Either screen all 17 qualifying candidates, or amend the registered plan to state the actual rule verbatim ('the 10 candidates in CANDIDATE_TARGETS, of which the 6 with the shortest receptor chains were run because of compute budget'), re-register with a new hash, and mark the existing result as a deviation. MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4      valid=True fcat=0.34 flagged=False ['lc3'] | Microglial Autophagosomal Membrane LC3-II
AstroZo1-Protect-A3        valid=False fcat=-1.00 flagged=False ['zo-1','occludin'] | BMEC Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) & Occludin Complex
AstroEos-NO-A1             valid=True fcat=0.09 flagged=False [] | Estrogen Receptor-β (ER-β) LBD (Glu305, Arg346)
AstroSuper-CBF-EAAT2-A5    valid=True fcat=0.10 flagged=False [] | ER-β LBD & EAAT2 Transporter Domain

findings.why_wrong: (1) ESR2/ER-β is a ligand-activated nuclear receptor: a peptide must cross the plasma membrane and enter the nucleus to reach its LBD. 'esr', 'estrogen', 'er-b' are not in CYTOPLASMIC_TARGETS, so AstroEos-NO-A1 and AstroSuper-CBF-EAAT2-A5 pass a gate whose whole purpose is to catch exactly this. (2) MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 targets LC3-II on the autophagosomal membrane — cytosolic, and inside a second membrane — but escapes because frac_cationic 0.34 >= 0.30 is treated as proof of a cell-penetrating mechanism. That threshold is not a validated CPP criterion, and even bona fide CPPs are overwhelmingly endosome-trapped; the neighbouring HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 at 0.27 is flagged for the same class of target, so the verdict turns on a 0.07 difference in Lys/Arg fraction. (3) AstroZo1-Protect-A3 names ZO-1 and occludin — both matched — but validate.py:131-132 returns early on an invalid sequence, so the most clear-cut compartment violation in the file is never reported. (4) The docstring at :31-35 presents EXTRACELLULAR_TARGETS as the basis of the check; it is dead code, so nothing ever verifies that a target claimed extracellular actually is. I found no false positives: all five current flags (X3/Keap1, X5/AMPK, P4/GSK-3, M2/Keap1, M5/Keap1) are biologically correct.
findings.fix: Add nuclear receptors and nuclear/organellar compartments to the keyword list (esr1, esr2, estrogen receptor, nr3c1, glucocorticoid receptor, nucleus, mitochond, lysosom, autophagosom). Replace the frac_cationic>=0.30 rule with an explicit, cited CPP-motif whitelist, or drop the exemption entirely and report 'target unreachable unless a delivery mechanism is declared'. Run the compartment check before the sequence-validity early return so records with ambiguous residues are still flagged. Either wire EXTRACELLULAR_TARGETS into a positive check or delete it and the docstring that references it.

findings.fix: Store CANDIDATE_TARGETS as a list of receptors per candidate, screen each declared arm separately, and record in the prespec exactly which arms were and were not modelled and why. findings.why_wrong: The repository is now public, and a public repository with no LICENSE defaults to all-rights-reserved, so no one may reuse the code, the curated dataset or the run artefacts — including the 145 Boltz-2 outputs and the pre-registered study code that the README invites readers to reproduce. This is a scan-level observation; a licensing specialist should confirm the redistribution terms per source.

unverified_concerns: Literature correctness of the retained mechanism claims that I could not test computationally. Ginsenoside Rg1 is asserted to 'bind the extracellular domain of TrkB to induce receptor dimerization' at Asp298/Glu319 (data/dataset.json:136-138); direct TrkB-D5 binding by Rg1 is not, to my knowledge, established — the better-supported account is glucocorticoid-receptor modulation with indirect BDNF/TrkB upregulation. Asiatic acid is asserted to bind the 'TrkB Transmembrane Region' (dataset.json:890), which for a pentacyclic triterpene acid would be a remarkable and, as far as I know, unreported binding mode. Huperzine A is asserted to act on the 'NMDA Channel' (dataset.json:14) — reported NMDA activity is in the high-micromolar-to-millimolar range and not pharmacologically comparable to its low-nanomolar AChE inhibition. I did not run a literature verification pass on these, so they are concerns rather than findings.

Huperzine A's class field reads 'Sesquiterpene Lycopodium Alkaloid' (data/dataset.json:13). Lycopodium alkaloids are lysine/acetate-derived, not terpenoid, so 'sesquiterpene' looks like a chemotaxonomic error, but I could not reproduce that with a tool in this environment.

Ginkgolide B's GABA_A Thr261 annotation (dataset.json binding_residues_text) is not checkable because no GABA-A subunit is in data/target_registry.json; the gate's four CHRM1 failures for this record are artefacts (SCI-01), so this residue is currently unassessed rather than assessed-and-passed.

check_residues validates a residue by identity-at-position, which passes cross-species annotations by coincidence roughly 5-9% of the time per token. README.md:253 acknowledges the Phe330 case explicitly, and I confirmed P22303 canonical position 330 is indeed Phe, so a Torpedo-numbered annotation passes the human check. With 45+ tokens, several further coincidental passes are expected. I did not estimate the false-pass rate quantitatively.

I did not re-run any Boltz-2 prediction, per instruction, so all ipTM/pLDDT values in data/study_*.json and runs/ are taken as given. The pseudoreplication in study #9 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 are the same sequence and are counted as two of six in mean_native_iptm and n_candidates_below_0.6) is disclosed in prose at README.md:432-437 and corrected explicitly in Slate #10, so I did not raise it as a finding — but the metric itself in data/study_candidate_screen.json is still computed over n=6 rather than 5 independent molecules.
I did not audit the ADMET, PRODIGY, pose-accuracy or corpus code paths, the memory ledger, or the other six pre-registered studies; those are outside this area.
what_is_sound: The curated natural-product chemistry is correct. I checked all eight InChIKeys against PubChem PUG-REST (https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/cid/854026,441923,11973122,5281605,969516,177827987,6451084,119034/property/InChIKey,MolecularFormula,Title/JSON) and every one matches the cited CID exactly, with the right compound title: Huperzine A ZRJBHWIHUMBLCN-YQEJDHNASA-N / C15H18N2O; Ginsenoside Rg1 YURJSTAIMNSZAE-HHNZYBFYSA-N / C42H72O14; Ginkgolide B SQOJOAFXDQDRGF-ZMVGXLHTSA-N / C20H24O10; Baicalein FXNFHKRTJBSTCS-UHFFFAOYSA-N / C15H10O5; Curcumin VFLDPWHFBUODDF-FCXRPNKRSA-N / C21H20O6; onjisaponin V MYKOTWPDDUNUJG-VNBMPPIYSA-N / C82H122O41; Salvianolic acid B SNKFFCBZYFGCQN-VWUOOIFGSA-N / C36H30O16; Asiatic acid JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UYDOISQJSA-N / C30H48O5. That is 8/8 — the single most defect-prone item in the original review is now clean.

The curation also silently fixed real errors: onjisaponin V's formula went from the legacy 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)' to the correct C82H122O41, and the legacy curcumin SMILES containing the illegal token 'OCH3' and the legacy salvianolic-acid-B 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)' were replaced with parseable isomeric structures. Stereochemistry is now fully defined where PubChem defines it.

Structural descriptions that I could test against the curated structures hold up. RDKit on the shipped SMILES: Ginkgolide B has 6 rings and exactly one tert-butyl group, matching 'rigid 6-ring cage structure with a tert-butyl moiety'; asiatic acid has 5 rings, matching 'ursane pentacyclic'; curcumin is a symmetric two-aryl diarylheptanoid, matching 'symmetrical diarylheptanoid'; salvianolic acid B has exactly 4 catechol matches, matching '4 catechol rings'.

The KLVFF / amyloid flagging is correct and, on this data, complete. Scanning all 35 sequences for eight canonical amyloid-nucleating segments (KLVFF, LVFFA, GAIIGLM, GGVVIA, VQIVYK, VQIINK, NFGAIL, NNQQNY) returns exactly two hits, BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 and CogAbeta-Clearer-08, and peptide.analyze flags both. No candidate with an aggregation-nucleating segment is missed.

The compartment check produces no false positives on the shipped data. All five flags — HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 and MicroDual-Trem2-Nrf2-M5 and MicroNrf2-AntiInflam-M2 (Keap1), HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5 (AMPK), PfcGsk-WntLinker-P4 (GSK-3β) — name genuinely cytosolic targets, and the reasoning ('an extracellular peptide with no penetrating mechanism cannot reach a cytosolic protein') is the right call in every case. The problem is under-detection (SCI-04), not over-detection.

The registry-based residue resolution is a genuinely good idea, well implemented at the single-target level. cbc/registry.py's TargetRecord.check_annotation correctly distinguishes canonical from mature numbering and returns an explicit verdict for each, which is exactly the right abstraction — e.g. ACHE Trp286 'resolves only in mature numbering', Phe330 'resolves only in canonical numbering', and the derived mixed_numbering_convention flag on HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 and BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 is a real and subtle catch. Only the string-to-target attribution layer (SCI-01) is broken.

The peptide developability liabilities are quantitatively triggered and biologically right. Every liability names its threshold and the mechanism (MW vs passive BBB diffusion, polycationic GAG binding and rapid clearance, cationic-amphipathic membrane lysis, odd-cysteine thiol scrambling, n!! disulfide pairings, serum-peptidase half-life at >=30 residues). The note that hERG models are outside their applicability domain for a multi-kDa polycation, and that membrane lysis and immunogenicity are the relevant liabilities for that modality, is exactly the right judgement and is stated in the data itself.

The retraction machinery works. Every one of the 25 candidates carries retracted_claims with the original affinity/safety string, a computed Kd-implied-by-stated-dG, the discrepancy in kcal/mol and in log10 units, and a verdict — and the frontend renders these as retractions, not results (app.js:341, :357, :370). The thermodynamic audit is correct arithmetic at 298.15 K.

The therapeutic and de-novo-design framing is genuinely gone from the public face. grep across README.md, index.html and app.js for 'therapeut|drug candidate|design(ed) peptide|de novo|lead compound|treatment for' returns only three hits, and all three are disclaimers or retrospective narration: README.md:23 and index.html:131 both say 'a hypothesis catalogue, not de novo designs', and README.md:435 describes what the platform *used to* claim. grep for the fabricated efficacy figures ('280%','350%','420%','310%','240%','Seizure Index') across README.md, index.html and app.js returns nothing — they survive only inside the JSON, which is why SCI-05 is MAJOR and not BLOCKER.

All six verification suites pass as designed, including the data gate correctly exiting 1 on the legacy data (./.venv/bin/python verify_all.py -> 'ALL 6 SUITES OK'), and platform/validate.py is deterministic in its counts (124 across 13 categories on every run).

The candidate screen's design is methodologically excellent and its reporting is honest about its own negatives: a per-candidate composition-matched null was the right construct, the pre-registered known_confounds correctly anticipated that three decoys cannot reach significance and that a negative bounds the pipeline rather than the biology, and README Slate #10 volunteers that the two candidates that beat their nulls are the same molecule, so the effective n is one. Very few projects report against themselves that carefully.
audits.verdict: The rebuild's chemistry layer is genuinely fixed — 8/8 InChIKeys verify against PubChem, the retraction and provenance machinery works, the peptide liability logic is sound, and the therapeutic framing is gone from the public face. Two problems are serious enough to block. First, the largest gate category is partly the gate's own artefact: check_residues applies one target's numbering to every residue token in a multi-target string, so at least 12 of the 45 'fabricated residue' calls are false — including Keap1 Tyr334 and Arg415, which I resolved against Q14145 and which are correct — while the flagship record, Huperzine A, has four genuine residue errors that are never checked at all because the target name lives in a field the gate does not read. The figure '45' is published in verify_all.py and the README as a result. Second, README.md:441 and the hash-locked prespec both state the candidate screen covered every candidate with a registry, extracellular receptor; 17 qualify and 6 were run, selected by an undeclared hand-written dict plus a receptor-length cut, and study #10 inherits the same selection. Below that: all retained mechanistic free text, including unretracted efficacy figures like 'LTP +280%' and 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' on a peptide that is literally Aβ(16-35), ships with no provenance envelope at all; the one marking that does exist is boilerplate that misdescribes 7 of 8 records; the compartment gate misses two nuclear-receptor targets, an autophagosomal one and a tight-junction one; and the two public faces contradict each other, with the web app announcing 'No structure prediction has been run in this repository' over a repo containing 145 Boltz-2 artefacts and a README badge advertising 91 gate violations against an actual 124. None of these is a return to fabrication — the failures now are stale synchronisation and a validator that overreaches on strings — but the four public-facing false statements should be fixed before the repository is cited.

findings.why_wrong: Both studies conclude the designed peptides fail to engage their declared targets, and README:372 states the negative is "evidence about the candidate, not the method". But the assay never presented the target site. _receptor_seq returns the whole UniProt CHAIN, which for a type-I single-pass receptor (TREM2) and a four-TM pentameric channel subunit (CHRNA7) includes the transmembrane helices and the entire intracellular region, modelled as a soluble monomer in vacuum; for AChE it appends the 40-residue C-terminal t-peptide/WAT helix that is absent from all 12 PDB entries the registry itself lists (4EY7/4M0E entity = 542 aa). Boltz then docks the peptides preferentially onto exactly those artefactual surfaces. The candidate literally named GorgeBlock makes zero contacts with any catalytic-gorge residue and puts 67% of its interface on the tail; the TREM2 "agonist" binds 100% cytoplasmic; the CHRNA7 "PAM" binds 100% cytoplasmic (the TM3-TM4 loop). CHRNA7's allosteric and orthosteric sites are additionally subunit-interface sites that do not exist in a monomer. The ipTM values, the native-vs-decoy comparisons and both empirical p-values are therefore about which shuffled peptide sticks best to a construct artefact - a wrong construct that, as the task hypothesised, depresses every candidate together and is indistinguishable from the reported result. The code's own stated inclusion rule (candidate_screen.py:56-58, "an intracellular target cannot be reached by a peptide with no penetrating mechanism") is contradicted by the construct it builds.
findings.fix: Replace _receptor_seq with a domain-aware constructor: for targets carrying a UniProt Transmembrane/Topological-domain annotation, emit only the extracellular topological domain (TREM2 19-174, CHRNA7 23-233); for AChE emit the catalytic domain (canonical 32-574 / mature 1-543, the span of 4EY7) and drop the t-peptide; record the chosen span and its justification in target_registry.json next to mature_offset. Add a post-prediction interface guard that computes contact residues and fails the run when >20% of the interface lies outside the declared target topological domain. Re-run #9 and #10 on corrected constructs before restating any conclusion about the candidates, and retract README:372/422/485 in the interim.

findings.why_wrong: H3 licenses a screen of designed 31-41mers against 212-583-residue receptors from a recovery rate measured on natural 7-17mers against 80-304-residue receptors - a set that violates the study's own registered exclusion criteria (peptide 5-30 aa, receptor 50-350 aa) in every single candidate. Three independent lines close the gate. (i) Domain: 0/6 candidate peptides and 1/6 receptors are inside the validated range, and the peptide class differs too (natural linear motifs binding canonical grooves - PDZ, LXXLL nuclear-receptor boxes, a trypsin inhibitor - versus designed Cys-rich chimeras with GGGGS linkers). (ii) Stratum choice: a designed sequence cannot be memorised, so the post-cutoff stratum, not the pre-cutoff one, is its analogue, and post-cutoff is 3/8 = 0.375, which fails the same >0.5 criterion; the study's own known_confound #3 already concedes the benchmark rate is "an OPTIMISTIC bound on what a screen of arbitrary designed peptides would achieve", which is precisely a statement that the gate statistic does not transfer. Three further pre-cutoff entries (4S15, 4XT9, 4Y29) share one recognition motif (the nuclear-receptor LXXLL box), reducing effective independence to roughly five systems.
findings.fix: Close the gate as stated and re-scope it. Either (a) restate H3's conclusion as applying only to natural peptides of 5-30 aa on receptors of 50-350 aa and declare study #9 out of domain, or (b) re-curate the benchmark to include 30-45 aa peptides and 200-600 aa receptors and re-measure. Enforce "one entry per receptor accession per stratum" by sequence identity (<90%) rather than by accession so the FimH pair cannot recur. Report Clopper-Pearson rather than Wilson intervals at n=8. Amend README.md:372 and data/study_candidate_screen.json:443 to state that the sensitivity demonstration was on a different peptide class and does not license reading #9's low scores as evidence about the candidates.

findings.why_wrong: A pre-registration declaring alpha = 0.05, n_comparisons = 3 and multiplicity_correction = "holm" promises frequentist error control. What is computed and published under the key "p_holm" is `0.0 if <point estimate crosses threshold> else 1.0`, run through a Holm loop. Multiplying 0.0 by K is still 0.0 and multiplying 1.0 by K saturates at 1.0, so the correction is arithmetically inert - no outcome of the Holm step can ever change a verdict. There is no sampling distribution, no type-I error rate, and no dependence on n: 7/8 and 700/800 produce the identical "p = 0.0". A public repository whose central selling point is hash-locked pre-registration therefore ships 17 values that read as p-values and are not. The real numbers differ materially where it matters most: the gate's genuine Holm-adjusted p is 0.0352, a hair under alpha rather than zero.
findings.fix: Replace each indicator with the test the hypothesis implies: scipy.stats.binomtest(k, n, p0, alternative='greater') for the proportion hypotheses (H1/H3 in peptide_interface, H3 in candidate_screen), a paired or one-sample test for the difference hypotheses, and a bootstrap or Fisher-z test against the registered bound (not against zero) for correlation hypotheses. Feed those into the existing Holm loop and re-emit every data/study_*.json analysis block. Where a hypothesis is genuinely a descriptive threshold with no test, rename the field from "p_holm" to "threshold_met" and emit a boolean so no reader mistakes it for inference.

Additionally, derive min_attainable_p from each hypothesis's declared test rather than from one study-level test_type, since this study mixes an exact proportion test with a rank correlation.

findings.why_wrong: The attack the task proposed - that a median absolute error and a median SD are different statistics - is real but cuts the other way, so H3's conclusion survives; two smaller defects remain. First, affinity_corrected.py:184-185 filters the dispersion list to entries where log10_sd is not None, dropping the two single-record compounds, while median_absolute_error_log10 is taken over all 14; the published ratio therefore divides a statistic on 14 compounds by a statistic on 12, and on a common 12 the ratio is 2.91x, not 2.4x. Second, three of the twelve SDs are exactly 0 because the compound has two identical ChEMBL records, and an SD of 0 from duplicate records is not a measurement of dispersion - it deflates the denominator. Restricting to compounds where dispersion is estimable (>=5 records) gives 2.16x. Correcting the scale mismatch the task raised - median|N(0,s)| = 0.6745s, so the model's median |error| implies SD 1.921 - gives 4.32x on a like-for-like SD basis, i.e. the published number is conservative. The direction is confirmed by a proper paired test the study never ran (Wilcoxon p = 0.00073; bootstrap 95% CI on the difference [0.154, 1.492]).
findings.fix: Compute med_err over the same compound set as med_disp; exclude compounds with n < 3 records from both sides, or impute a literature dispersion floor for them and say which; state the ratio on a single scale - either both as medians of absolute deviations (multiply the reference SD by 0.6745) or both as SDs - and label it. Add the Wilcoxon paired test and the bootstrap CI to the metrics block so H3 rests on a test rather than on two point estimates. Update README:394-397 with the corrected ratio and its interval.

unverified_concerns: Whether Boltz-2's actual training cutoff corresponds to the 2023-05-31 split used to define study #7's strata. The study itself lists this as known_confound #2 ("Boltz's split is not published"); I could not verify it, so the pre/post contrast remains a proxy for memorisation rather than a measurement of it.

Whether re-running studies #9/#10 on corrected extracellular-only constructs would change their verdicts. Re-running Boltz was out of scope per the audit brief, so F1 establishes that the published conclusion is unsupported, not that the candidates would succeed on a correct construct.

Whether the AChE C-terminal t-peptide is modelled as an exposed amphipathic helix or as disordered coil in these particular Boltz outputs. I measured only contact frequency (53% of interface area on 6.9% of the construct, 7.8x enrichment), not the secondary structure or solvent exposure of the tail.

Licensing, attribution and redistribution exposure for the now-public repository: I did not examine LICENSE, the redistribution of PDB/ChEMBL/UniProt-derived content in data/ and runs/, or the terms of the vendored DockQ, PRODIGY, PoseBusters and ADMET-AI dependencies. The brief flagged this as raised-stakes and it deserves a separate pass.

Whether the four duplicated sequences in data/extracted_raw.json indicate a broader provenance problem in the candidate corpus (for example codes assigned to targets they were never designed against). I confirmed the duplicates exist but did not trace their origin.
I did not execute verify_all.py or the 113 platform tests, so the README's "6 verification suites all passing" claim is unchecked here.
what_is_sound: The ipTM/DockQ calibration in study #7 is NOT driven by extreme points - the attack fails cleanly. Full rho = 0.8471 (p = 3.47e-05, n = 16). Dropping the top and bottom point by ipTM (31EE, 4XOJ) gives rho = 0.8242, p = 2.9e-04; by DockQ (31EE, 4XT9) gives 0.8154, p = 3.8e-04; dropping the union of all four extremes (n = 13) gives 0.8132, p = 7.2e-04. Exhaustive 2-point deletion over all 120 pairs: the worst case is rho = 0.7714, p = 0.00123 (dropping 4S15 and 31EE). Jackknife-1 range 0.8143-0.9000. One caveat worth recording rather than a refutation: the bootstrap 95% CI is [0.545, 0.964], so P(rho <= the registered 0.6 bar) = 0.045. Reproduced with <SP>/a1_spearman.py.

Study #6's 7 misses are NOT an artefact of the pocket-alignment procedure - this attack also fails. I re-fitted a separate Kabsch transform per reference ligand copy, with the 10 A pocket shell defined from that copy alone, and re-scored with the same symmetry-corrected CalcRMS. Every published RMSD reproduces: 23SI 8.493 -> 8.457, 25VX 8.099 -> 7.547, 13LV 17.436 -> 17.438, all others identical to 3 dp. Hits stay 5/12 and no verdict changes. The sequence-based residue pairing (posebench.py:236-240) and the guard refusing to pair residues of differing type are correct, and the two previously-fixed scoring bugs documented in README:325-335 are genuine fixes. Reproduced with <SP>/a7_realign.py.

Study #8's H3 ("the model is the larger error term") is robust to every reformulation I attempted, including the one the task proposed. Converting both quantities to the same scale makes the gap larger, not smaller (4.32x rather than 2.4x); restricting to compounds with estimable dispersion keeps it at 2.02-2.41x; a proper paired Wilcoxon that the study never ran gives p = 0.00073 with a bootstrap 95% CI on the difference of [0.154, 1.492]. Even subtracting reference variance from observed variance leaves the model term dominant. The conclusion stands and is understated.

The DockQ acceptability threshold is not load-bearing for study #7's gate: at CAPRI acceptable (0.23) the pre-cutoff stratum is 7/8, at CAPRI medium (0.49) it is 5/8, at CAPRI high (0.80) it is 5/8 - all above 0.5. The gate fails for the reasons in F2, not because 0.23 was chosen leniently.

The pipeline is genuinely deterministic at fixed seed. The duplicate candidate pair returned ipTM values identical to full float precision (0.7588154673576355 in study #10, 0.3402 in study #9) across independent invocations, and the pose and peptide studies reproduce from stored artefacts. This is a real, checkable property most comparable projects lack.

The structural artefacts are retained and re-analysable. /tmp/cbc_screen, /tmp/cbc_msa10, /tmp/cbc_pose and /tmp/cbc_pep hold the full Boltz outputs and runs/ holds 145 content-addressed files, which is what made every finding here reproducible without re-running a single prediction. Findings F1 and F5 exist only because the coordinates were kept.

The mmCIF numbering convention is self-consistent and verifiable: parsed receptor chain lengths match the registry mature-chain lengths exactly (583 ACHE, 480 CHRNA7, 212 TREM2), and on the near-perfect 4XOJ prediction (DockQ 0.952) my independent contact parser recovers the trypsin active site - construct positions 64 (His of AAHC), 104, 200 (catalytic Ser of GDSGGP) and the 214-220 substrate loop.

The prespec module's reachability guard (platform/cbc/prespec.py:139-171) is a genuinely good idea, correctly implemented, and would have caught study #7's underpowered design had the test type been declared honestly (see F4). The same file's check that not all hypotheses share one predicted_by is a thoughtful safeguard against non-discriminating designs.

README:485-489 discloses the study #10 duplicate, states the effective independent count is one, and gives the correct empirical p of 0.091 - the disclosure is present and accurate even though the metrics block was not recomputed (F6). README:322-329 correctly flags H2 in study #6 as underpowered rather than null, and README:333-340 admits the receptor-disjoint stratum could not be built. This is above-median candour.
audits.verdict: Two of the six proposed attacks succeed decisively, one succeeds partially, and three fail - and the failures matter as much as the successes. The ipTM calibration (rho 0.847) survives every deletion I could construct (worst 2-point deletion 0.771, p = 0.0012), study #6's misses survive a full per-copy re-alignment unchanged, and study #8's H3 survives every rescaling and gets stronger under a proper paired test. Those three conclusions are sound. The two that fail are load-bearing. First, studies #9 and #10 do not show that the candidates fail: the mature-chain construct hands Boltz the transmembrane and intracellular regions of TREM2 and CHRNA7 and the 40-residue t-peptide of AChE, and the peptides dock there - the TREM2 native interface is 100% cytoplasmic, the CHRNA7 native is 100% cytoplasmic, 38 of 43 AChE folds touch no gorge residue, and the candidate named GorgeBlock puts 67% of its interface on a tail absent from every deposited AChE structure. Every ipTM, every native-vs-decoy comparison and both empirical p-values in those studies describe a construct artefact - exactly the uniform confound the task hypothesised. Second, study #7's gate should not have opened: not one of the six candidates has a peptide length inside the range #7 validated (31-41 aa versus 7-17 aa, against a registered exclusion of 5-30 aa), five of six receptors are outside it, the unmemorisable stratum fails the same >0.5 bar at 3/8, the exact CI on 7/8 contains 0.5, and collapsing a 98.9%-identical duplicate pair leaves 6/7 at p = 0.0625. The duplicate attack on #10 flips the reported effect's sign (+0.0186 to -0.0105) and halves n_candidates_beating_all_decoys, but no verdict changes. Underneath all of this sits a systematic issue the task did not ask about: 17 of 21 published p_holm values are 0.0/1.0 indicator functions rather than p-values, and study #7's test_type was declared "parametric" for what are exact binomial proportions - the one field that disables the platform's own reachability guard, which on the honest declaration returns UNREACHABLE VERDICT. The project's instincts are good, its artefact retention is what made this audit possible, and its README is unusually candid; but the inferential plumbing needs replacing with real tests, and the two construct-dependent conclusions should be retracted until the receptors are built correctly.

Item #10 was run at 6 of 26 sequences, K=10 instead of K>=199, no off-target panel, and a per-candidate p floor of 0.091 that its own first success criterion forbids; item #6's physical-validity component was registered and explicitly not executed, and its third stratum does not exist. The msa-specificity prespec goes further and pre-emptively rejects the per-candidate empirical p as unreachable at K=10 ('the empirical p has a hard floor of 1/(N+1); at N=10 that floor is 0.091 ... exactly the defect this project's registration module rejects'), which is precisely the reasoning MEM-01 says the slate-complete sentence abandons.
audits.verdict:
The CBC-Memory ledger is structurally sound and substantially truthful. The mechanics do what they claim: 74/74 tests pass, a forced rebuild reproduces the index bit-for-fact (stats and all four views identical), git proves zero deleted lines across every commit touching memory/ledger/, and there are no duplicate ids, no dangling edges, no dangling status targets, and no unresolvable evidence references. On the two questions the brief put most sharply: every one of the 81 VERIFIED claims does have resolving supporting evidence (81/81, via STATUS.evidence -- my first pass looked only at edges and was wrong), and of ~45 claims I checked against their artefacts, the numbers are there. The dG-docs claim that was later retracted was NOT deleted.

Where it fails is at the seam between prose and machinery. Corrections are written as narrative but never wired: there are zero SUPERSEDED and zero WITHDRAWN status records in a ledger containing three explicit retractions and four REFUTES edges, three of whose targets still read ASSERTED, and v_dispute consults only status records so disputes.md prints "_No disputes._" over a ledger full of recorded disagreement (MEM-03). Two of the three named corrections cite an "earlier claim in this ledger" that git proves was never written there, making the withdrawal unauditable (MEM-04). The public view flattens 50 of 81 CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION verifications into the same unqualified checkmark as the 25 confirmed as written (MEM-02). And the one residual public overclaim is README.md:491, "The slate is complete. All 11 consensus items have now been executed," which is false for item #10 (6 of 26 sequences, K=10 against a required K>=199, no off-target panel) and item #6 (PoseBusters arm NOT_TESTED, receptor-disjoint stratum non-existent) -- both documented in the project's own artefacts three lines above the sentence (MEM-01).

No BLOCKER. Nothing I found is a fabricated number, a wrong scientific result, or a legal exposure. Four MAJORs, five MINORs, one NIT. The failure mode this project exists to prevent -- a ledger asserting a number its artefact does not contain -- occurs three times (MEM-05, MEM-06, MEM-07) and each time it is a misstated interval or an unbacked pilot figure that leaves the conclusion intact, not an invented result. Fix README.md:491 first; it is the only defect a reader of the public repo can be misled by without opening the ledger.

The four candidates missing `length`, `cysteines` and `disulfide_connectivity` (HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4, AstroZo1-Protect-A3, AstroPafr-Block-A4, CogWnt-Fzd-09) are exactly the four with valid=false, and app.js:316 renders that grid only inside the `c.valid ?` branch — so the gap is by construction, not a break. No dangling field reference exists.

Slate #9 reproduces from its own artefact. Recomputing native vs best-decoy ipTM from data/study_candidate_screen.json confirms beats_null=False for all six candidates and mean native 0.405 against mean decoy 0.411 — the designed sequences do score marginally worse than shuffles of their own residues, exactly as claimed. Reporting that in a public README is the single most credible thing in the repository.

The provenance-rendering discipline in app.js is intact and enforced. renderValue (app.js:~45-66) is the only path from a value to the DOM, and it emits "not computed" or "illustrative only" labels rather than numbers for those statuses; verify_frontend.py independently regression-tests that the four fabricated legacy renderers (the sin-based pLDDT formula, the PAE ramp, the charCode geometry, the 'REAL FASTA' comment) are gone, and each check passes.

Attribution and trademark hygiene on the page itself is correct. Every DeepMind mention in index.html is a disclaimer or trademark notice, there is no Google logo badge, no "Live Connected" badge, no "designed via AlphaFold3", and both CDN script tags are version-pinned (chart.js@4.4.7, 3dmol@2.4.2) with a comment explaining why pinning matters.

The README's scientific reasoning sections hold up as written — the three-ground argument against emitting ΔG from the pooled affinity head, the Cheng–Prusoff bias calculation, the sign error it catches, and the honest statement that Slate #11 cannot separate "PRODIGY cannot discriminate" from "these interfaces are not real". These are the writing of someone reporting against their own hypothesis, and the Known limitations section ends with "No wet-lab validation of anything."
audits.verdict:
The science in this repository is in far better shape than its public face. Every quantitative claim I re-derived from the artefacts — the head-to-head pLDDT table, the 2.66-unit noise floor, the Slate #9 native-vs-decoy screen — reproduced exactly, and the README reports negative results against the author's own stated hypotheses. That is the hard part, and it is done.

The public face has not kept up, and it has failed in the one direction nobody checks for: understatement. The page a visitor lands on opens with "No structure prediction has been run in this repository" while 145 Boltz-2 artefacts sit in runs/ and the README asserts the opposite in bold. All 35 candidates are labelled `not_computed` with the note "No structure prediction has been run for this sequence", though 22 of them have real Boltz-2 pLDDT committed — including the −46.19 delta that is the project's headline finding. The Overview tab tells the reader the workbench runs no structure predictor and performs no ADMET, both false. And verify_frontend.py:116 requires the false sentence to remain, so making the page honest currently breaks the build — the exact staleness trap the same file's README check already fixed, with a comment explaining it, thirteen lines below.

Three public numbers are wrong: the gate badge says 91 violations against a live 124, the studies badge says 7 against 8, and data/validation_gate.json — the file the Validation tab actually fetches — is frozen at 91 with fabricated_residue 11 instead of 45, breaking the page's own printed promise that "Every count below is reproducible from a clean checkout."

Two items raise real stakes now that the repo is public. There is no LICENSE file, the badge says "private research", and ChEMBL-derived records are redistributed in four data files with no licence or attribution statement anywhere. And Node.js — an undeclared dependency — makes the documented "run everything" command die with a raw traceback on a clean machine.

On the mistakable-for-a-validated-result question: yes, one surface remains. The Candidates tab renders each sequence under an asserted mechanism name — "AChE Gorge Clamper", "Presenegenin Dual Super-Drug", "α7 nAChR Allosteric Modulator" — with a green "sequence valid" pill, a full property grid, and a Copy FASTA button, while the studies showing that those same molecules do not beat a composition-matched shuffle of their own residues are nowhere in the UI. Eight pre-registered studies, nine result files, 145 artefacts, and the front end surfaces none of them. Fixing that is the highest-value change available: it would replace the last overclaim with the strongest evidence the project has.

Twelve findings: two BLOCKER, seven MAJOR, two MINOR, one NIT. All reproduced; the index.html edit used to demonstrate DOC-03 was reverted and the tree is as I found it.

Reproduced. inference_variance.py:141-145 confirmed_if = '|mean(with MSA) - mean(without MSA)| < the pooled across-seed SD from H1, and the paired t-test across candidates does not reject at Holm-adjusted 0.05'; variance_analysis.py:137-138 gates on `adj[2] >= 0.05`. Holm is monotone non-decreasing in p, so under a >= alpha acceptance rule it can only make confirmation easier -- the correction is used anti-conservatively. The ache H3 arm also reproduces: ache_affinity_benchmark.py:228-229 sets the verdict from `abs(z) <= 2` alone while p3 sits in the Holm family and is printed beside the hypothesis (huperzine_z 0.94, p_holm H3 0.81407, verdict CONFIRMED). The observed behaviour reproduces (`returned 0.009900990099009901 / true BH floor 0.19801980198019803 / check() [] / _n_needed() 20`) but the statistical claim behind it is wrong, and the proposed fix would introduce a defect. min_attainable_p is documented at prespec.py:115 as 'Smallest adjusted p-value this design could ever produce' -- a minimum over all possible data. BH-adjusted p-values are a step-UP procedure with a cumulative min from the largest rank down: p_adj_(1) = min over j>=1 of (K/j)*p_(j), which is <= K*p_(1), not equal to it. I verified with my own BH implementation: with all 20 tests at the permutation floor 1/101, `all 20 at floor -> BH adj: [0.00990099 0.00990099 0.00990099]` -- i.e. the minimum attainable BH-adjusted p is exactly 1/101 = 0.00990099, precisely what the code returns. The auditor's '0.198' is BH's adjusted value in the single-signal configuration (`one at floor rest 1.0 -> BH adj[0]: 0.19801980198019803`), which is the worst case, not the minimum. So the plan IS reachable and check() is right to pass it. Applying the proposed fix (adding 'bh' to the tuple at prespec.py:135) would make the module refuse to register genuinely reachable BH designs, and would additionally desynchronise the error message, because `_n_needed()` at prespec.py:173-175 carries the same ('bonferroni','holm') tuple and returned 20 in my run -- so the UNREACHABLE message would tell the author to raise B to 20 when B=100 was already sufficient. A wrong fix, and worse than no finding. The only residual is a NIT: the docstring at prespec.py:124-125 should say explicitly why BH is exempt, so the omission does not read as an oversight.

Reproduced exactly: at B=399, K=20, holm, alpha=0.05 -> `min_attainable_p 0.05 / check() [] / _n_needed() 400`; at B=400 -> `pmin 0.04987531172069826, check []`. I also confirmed the equality is exact in floating point, not a display artefact: `(1.0/400)*20 == 0.05` returns True. The internal inconsistency is real -- prespec.py:150 uses `pmin > self.alpha` while `_n_needed()` at :173-177 computes int(k/alpha - 1) + 1 = 400, i.e. it treats B=399 as insufficient. Every registered decision rule is a strict inequality (verified at ache_affinity_benchmark.py:90 'Holm-adjusted p < 0.05'), so at pmin == alpha the test can never fire. Changing line 150 to `pmin >= self.alpha` is correct and makes check() exactly consistent with _n_needed() at the boundary in both directions. The suggested regression test is the right one.

The observation reproduces: `grep -h ... prespec/*.json` shows all eight files with "test_type": "parametric", "min_attainable_p": 0.0, "n_comparisons": 3, "multiplicity_correction": "holm". Two corrections to the reasoning and the fix. (1) The headline remedy does not do what it claims. I ran min_attainable_p under both declarations: `parametric min_attainable_p = 0.0 check []` and `none min_attainable_p = 0.0 check []`. prespec.py:127-133 routes both 'parametric' and 'none' to the same else branch (raw_min = 0.0), so re-registering four studies as test_type='none' -- a costly change that rotates four hash-locked plan files -- changes min_attainable_p by exactly nothing. The substantive part of the fix is the new check() rule (flag test_type=='none' with multiplicity_correction!='none') plus honest labelling; that part is correct and cheap. (2) 'Vacuous for every study' is overstated. For ache-affinity (two Spearman tests), msa-specificity (paired t) and peptide-interface (Spearman), the genuine tests really are parametric, and raw_min = 0 is a defensible approximation of a floor that is astronomically small at n=14-16 -- the reachability check is uninformative there, not wrong. The charge lands squarely only on the four threshold-decision studies (candidate-screen, affinity-corrected, pose-accuracy, prodigy-discrimination), which is still worth fixing.

Reproduced exactly: contrib {'ic_cc': 0.1863, 'ic_ca': 0.5533, 'ic_pp': 0.1196, 'ic_pa': 0.7752, 'nis_apolar': 0.1279, 'nis_charged': 0.0663}; sum of SDs 1.828713232622619; nis frac 0.10620031002123416 vs reported 0.1062; actual between-candidate SD of dG 1.4098093694302563. prodigy_falsification.py:224-229 confirms `total = sum(contrib.values())` where each contrib is a stdev of a signed term, so the denominator is a sum of standard deviations of correlated signed quantities. It is neither a variance nor equal to the SD it purports to decompose (1.8287 vs 1.4098), so 'accounts for only 10.6% of the between-candidate variance' (README:282) claims a decomposition property the quantity does not have. Reproduced exactly: n 15, self-inclusive z 0.9399548418841595 (repo huperzine_z 0.94), leave-one-out z 1.0050333049199422. ache_affinity_benchmark.py:203-204 confirms `z = (hup_err - err.mean()) / err.std(ddof=1)` with err including Huperzine A. No multiplicity correction exists across studies, only within them. Every prespec declares n_comparisons: 3 (verified: `grep -h '"n_comparisons"' prespec/*.json` returns "n_comparisons": 3 eight times) and each module runs its own independent 3-member Holm loop, so the 24 hypotheses of the programme are corrected as eight families of three rather than as one family. Several hypotheses are near-restatements across studies on overlapping data -- candidate-screen H2 'natives beat decoys on average' and msa-specificity H1 'natives separate from decoys' are the same claim on the same six candidates with 3 vs 10 decoys -- so the families are not independent either. Nothing published changes (the shared verdicts are FALSIFIED in both cases, and Holm within-family is already the conservative direction relative to no correction), but a README that leads on multiplicity discipline should state the family boundary it chose and why.

Reproduced across ALL 24 archived runs, not just three: `for r in sorted(glob('runs/*/')): PR.load(r)` gives source='mmcif_only', ptm=None, iptm=None, ranking=None, pae_None=True for every one — 'mmcif_only count: 24 of 24'. glob('runs/0083b1c7d3e6/confidence_*.json') -> [] and glob('.../pae_*.npz') -> [] while the directory actually contains boltz_results_input_predictions_input_confidence_input_model_0.json and ..._pae_input_model_0.npz. I traced the renaming to platform/rescue_runs.py:103: `out = target / rel.name if len(rel.parts)==1 else target / '_'.join(rel.parts)` — the archiver flattens boltz_results_input/predictions/input/confidence_... into one underscore-joined name, past the anchored globs at predictor.py:310/390/396. The unread JSON for runs/919fef2194e3 is {'confidence_score': 0.886..., 'ptm': 0.949..., 'iptm': 0.714...}, matching the finding's quoted numbers (the finding attributed them to the first-listed run; they belong to 919fef2194e3 — a labelling slip, not a substantive error). Two nuances the finding overstates slightly: the shipped study's ptm/iptm did NOT come from predictor.load — inference_variance.py:177 reads them from the runner's own `r.get('confidence')` dict — so no shipped ptm/iptm is affected. interface_pae IS affected: inference_variance.py:188 calls pred.interface_pae(...), 15 of 87 shipped rows carry interface_pae_min, and those were produced against the native /tmp/cbc_variance/.../predictions/input/ layout where the globs still matched. Re-running against runs/ would silently drop them. THE PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG. `d.glob('*confidence*.json')` also matches AlphaFold3's `*summary_confidences*.json`, and `if boltz_conf: _load_boltz(...)` at predictor.py:331 runs unconditionally regardless of source. I demonstrated the regression on a synthetic AF3 directory: TODAY 'source= alphafold3 ptm= 0.81 iptm= 0.66 ranking= 0.77'; with the widened glob also feeding _load_boltz, 'ptm= 0.81 iptm= 0.66 ranking= None' — _load_boltz overwrites ranking_score with data.get('confidence_score'), a key AF3 does not use, silently destroying a correct value. The fix must exclude summary_confidences (e.g. glob '*confidence*.json' then filter out names containing 'summary_confidences'), or gate the _load_boltz call on source == 'boltz'. The '*pde*' exclusion the fix calls for is unnecessary — 'pde' cannot match the pattern '*pae*' — but harmless.

Both halves reproduced with my own files (/tmp/v/n04.py). CASE A, four residues written at auth_seq_id 100/'.', 100/'A', 100/'B', 101/'.': 'parse_mmcif residues: 2 [(\'H\', 100, \'ALA\'), (\'H\', 101, \'ALA\')]' — two of four collapsed by the (chain, seq_id) `seen` set at predictor.py:273-275. Downloading 1IGY (an antibody with Kabat insertion codes) from RCSB: residues 52/52A and 82/82A/82B/82C exist in chains B and D. physics.parse_all_atoms merges them, giving n_residues 1304 against a true 1312 (8 lost), and check_bonds emits four spurious peptide-bond outliers that do not exist in the deposited file: {'residue': 'B/51-52', 'bond': 'C-N', 'length': 4.804, 'deviation_sigma': 150.8}, {'residue': 'B/81-82', 'length': 8.373, 'deviation_sigma': 305.9}, and the same pair for chain D. That is a wrong number produced from a real RCSB mmCIF, which strengthens the finding beyond what was claimed. None of the 16 pose-benchmark entries has a non-blank insertion code (I checked every one: LOST=0 for all 16), so the shipped study data is unaffected — consistent with the finding. Fix is correct; the PDB column index 26 (0-based) it names is the right one for the insertion-code field.

Reproduced against the cached O00206 record (/tmp/v/n0506.py, offset 23): residue_at(10,'canonical') -> 'T'; residue_at(10,'mature') -> 'V'; residue_at(10,'auth') -> 'V'; and I extended the probe — residue_at(10,'garbage') -> 'V', residue_at(10,'AUTH') -> 'V', residue_at(10,'') -> 'V'. Reproduced verbatim against O00206 (offset 23): 'canonical   1 -> mature  -22   residue_at(mature)=\'M\'   true canonical residue=\'M\''; 'canonical  23 -> mature    0   residue_at(mature)=\'P\'   true canonical residue=\'P\''; 'canonical  24 -> mature    1   residue_at(mature)=\'E\''. convert() at registry.py:120 applies the offset with no domain check, and residue_at() at line 110 adds it straight back, so the out-of-domain index lands inside the sequence and returns a plausible letter for a position that does not exist in mature numbering.
